Numerical checks of a posterior fit

Source: R/accessors.R
check_numerics.Rd

Reports the checks of the integration over the between-site standard deviation: the agreement of the rule with two other rules, the bounds on the omitted upper tail, and the location of the peak of the dispersion found at two resolutions.

Usage

check_numerics(x)

Arguments

x

An object of class reliability_posterior.

Value

A data frame with the columns check, value, limit and status ("ok" or "outside").

Details

For the node rule, the normalizing constant and the posterior means of \(I\) and \(H\) are compared with those of a rule whose panels are all halved, and with those of a rule whose lowest panel ends at half the value. The differences are relative, and their limit is \(10^{-10}\), or \(64J\) times the machine epsilon when that is larger, because the log density is a sum of \(J\) terms. For the adaptive engine, the check is the error estimate of stats::integrate() for the normalizing constant. The bounds on the omitted upper tail are those of Appendix D.3 of Lee (2026), extended to the mean model and to the priors of sd_prior(); the bound for \(E(\sigma_\tau^q)\) is shown divided by \(\sqrt{\mathrm{GM}(v)}^q\), so that it does not depend on the units. The bounds concern the numerical approximation, not the calibration of the posterior. The last row compares the peak of \(H\), where the mean reliability equals \(I\), as located by scans of the logit of \(I\) at two resolutions. vignette("implementation") has the details.

References

Lee, J. (2026). The geometry of informativeness: A Bregman-centroid diagnostic for partial pooling in multisite trials. Unpublished manuscript.

Examples

fit <- reliability_posterior(estimate, se = se, data = eight_schools)
check_numerics(fit)
#>                                                             check        value
#> 1     normalizing constant, rule against halved panels (relative) 0.000000e+00
#> 2            E(I) and E(H), rule against halved panels (relative) 1.214135e-16
#> 3           normalizing constant, lower end moved down (relative) 0.000000e+00
#> 4                  E(I) and E(H), lower end moved down (relative) 0.000000e+00
#> 5                               mass beyond the upper end (bound) 1.815325e-33
#> 6 E(sigma_tau^1) beyond the upper end, over sqrt(GM(v))^1 (bound) 7.171246e-28
#> 7 E(sigma_tau^2) beyond the upper end, over sqrt(GM(v))^2 (bound) 2.950961e-22
#> 8 E(sigma_tau^4) beyond the upper end, over sqrt(GM(v))^4 (bound) 6.396041e-11
#> 9            turning points of H at two resolutions (logit scale) 7.355228e-16
#>   limit status
#> 1 1e-10     ok
#> 2 1e-10     ok
#> 3 1e-10     ok
#> 4 1e-10     ok
#> 5 1e-12     ok
#> 6 1e-10     ok
#> 7 1e-10     ok
#> 8 1e-10     ok
#> 9 1e-07     ok
